questions.question: What is TypeScript?
questions.correct_answer: A typed superset of JavaScript that compiles to plain JavaScript, adding static type checking.

questions.question: Why use TypeScript?
questions.correct_answer: To catch errors during development, improve code readability, enable better tooling, and make refactoring safer.

questions.question: What is the difference between TypeScript and JavaScript?
questions.correct_answer: TypeScript adds static types, interfaces, enums, and generics. JavaScript is dynamically typed.

questions.question: How do you install TypeScript?
questions.correct_answer: npm install -g typescript or as a dev dependency: npm install -D typescript.

questions.question: What is the tsconfig.json file?
questions.correct_answer: The TypeScript configuration file that defines compiler options, file inclusion, and project settings.

questions.question: What does the 'any' type do?
questions.correct_answer: Disables type checking for a variable, allowing it to hold any value. Use sparingly as it defeats the purpose of TypeScript.

questions.question: What is type inference?
questions.correct_answer: TypeScript automatically determining the type of a variable based on its assigned value.

questions.question: What is the difference between unknown and any?
questions.correct_answer: unknown forces you to check the type before using it. any bypasses all type checking.

questions.question: What is a union type?
questions.correct_answer: A type that can be one of several types, defined with the | operator: string | number.

questions.question: What is a type assertion?
questions.correct_answer: Telling the compiler to treat a value as a specific type: value as string or <string>value.

questions.question: What is an interface in TypeScript?
questions.correct_answer: A way to define the shape of an object — its properties, methods, and types.

questions.question: What is the difference between type and interface?
questions.correct_answer: Interfaces are extendable with extends and can be merged. Types are more flexible (unions, intersections) but can't be merged.

questions.question: When should you use interface over type?
questions.correct_answer: Use interface for object shapes that may need extension or declaration merging. Use type for unions, intersections, or computed types.

questions.question: Can you extend an interface?
questions.correct_answer: Yes, using the extends keyword: interface B extends A { ... }.

questions.question: Can you extend a type?
questions.correct_answer: Not directly with extends, but you can use intersection types: type B = A & { extra: string }.

questions.question: What is declaration merging?
questions.correct_answer: When TypeScript combines multiple interface declarations with the same name into one. Types don't support this.

questions.question: What is a generic type?
questions.correct_answer: A type that accepts type parameters, like Array<T> or Box<T>, allowing reusable type-safe code.

questions.question: What is a mapped type?
questions.correct_answer: A type created by transforming properties of an existing type, e.g., { [K in keyof T]: boolean }.

questions.question: What is a conditional type?
questions.correct_answer: A type that selects one of two types based on a condition: T extends U ? X : Y.

questions.question: What is the utility type Partial<T>?
questions.correct_answer: Makes all properties of type T optional.
